gaps.note: an edit hides the transition to Kevin re-entering the negotiation after exiting

stage_a.note: Kanz displays very strong positive expression and enthusiastic body language while explaining the solution.
Kanz speaks with pronounced and sustained engagement and excitement when discussing catching live bait.
Both founders present with friendly, approachable smiles and courteous introductions to the panel.

venture.description: A rechargeable, robotic fishing lure that swims like a real fish to attract catches without live bait.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz and Sobhan introduce themselves, ask for their investment, detail the problems with traditional fishing, and demonstrate their robotic lure.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin comments on how much one can learn on Shark Tank, finding the product amazing.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark agrees with Kevin's sentiment about learning new things.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks Daymond if the robotic lure is different from anything he has ever used for fishing.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond answers Lori, noting rust issues with older lures, and asks the founders how often the unit needs replacing.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan states that the lure can currently be used about forty times while actively catching fish.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks how long the robotic lure can hold a battery charge.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz explains the charge times for the different sizes, ranging from forty-five minutes to two hours.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert asks what makes the founders fish experts and why he should believe them.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan states that he works as a project manager at manufacturing facilities.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz adds that he is a licensed professional counselor working in community mental health.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert jokes that their non-fishing backgrounds make perfect sense for a fishing company.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan describes his childhood fishing with his dad, his dad's illness, and his immigrant parents' sacrifices to explain their motivation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks where the founders originally came from.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan and Kanz reply that their family came from Iran.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks about the manufacturing costs, the retail prices, and their total sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz provides the landed costs for the mini and classic sizes, addressing only the cost part of the question.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks for the manufacturing cost of the new, larger saltwater lure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz states the cost of the large lure and then provides the retail prices for all three sizes.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks whether their sales are entirely direct-to-consumer or if they are in retail stores.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz explains that sales are mostly online, but they are in some small shops and have a Canadian distributor.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin asks about their presence in major outdoor retail chains.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan replies that getting into major retail chains is precisely why they are seeking an investor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz adds that the major chains would definitely answer a call from the investors.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin points out that their valuation implies they must be selling a large volume of lures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz provides their year-to-date sales figures and shares their revenue projections for the current and following year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if the company is currently profitable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz confirms they are making money, noting they both work full-time jobs, have no debt, and self-funded the start.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark praises them for being serious and efficient with their startup capital.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz adds that they reinvest every cent earned back into the company rather than paying themselves.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks if the two founders own the company in equal shares.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz confirms that they are equal partners in the business.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin suggests they could market the lures as an aquarium display rather than for fishing.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori jokes that an aquarium display would not require feeding.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark agrees that it would be a good idea for a restaurant setting.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert also agrees that it is a good idea.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond adds his agreement, calling it a great idea.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan concedes that the aquarium suggestion is indeed a clever and good idea.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark explains he is not a fisherman and lacks a feel for the product, so he exits.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan thanks Mark for his time and understanding.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori states she is also not a fisherman and considers the investment too early for her, exiting.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin argues they are essentially a product rather than a company, asking how he would recoup his investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz replies that business relies heavily on connections, and they value Kevin's extensive network to secure distribution.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin explains the work required to get retail distribution, demanding either a large equity share or a royalty to compensate.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori points out to the founders that Kevin is clearly looking for a royalty deal.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin playfully asks Lori if she just mentioned a royalty deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark laughs at Kevin's predictable move toward a royalty structure.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond also reacts humorously to Kevin's royalty hint.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan begins to suggest a counter to Kevin's demands.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin interrupts to make a formal offer: the requested cash for equity, plus a per-unit royalty until a cap.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert tells the founders that Kevin's proposition is a great offer.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan agrees with Robert that the offer is indeed a good one.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Robert disagrees with their philosophy about connections, emphasizing hard work instead, and exits because he feels they aren't ready.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan thanks Robert for his feedback and time.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond praises the product but exits due to the high valuation, noting the massive sales needed to recoup the investment.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin points out he is the only remaining investor and asks for their decision on his offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz counters Kevin's offer by proposing a higher investment amount for a larger equity stake.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori interrupts to clarify if their counter-offer includes any royalty component.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan confirms that their counter-offer removes the royalty entirely.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin rejects the counter-offer, scolds them for making a poor counter when an investor is interested, and demands better negotiation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Lori asks the founders directly if they are willing to accept a royalty deal structure.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz checks with his partner if they should discuss a royalty arrangement.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan agrees they should discuss the possibility of a royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Kanz offers a new counter, keeping the original equity but reducing both the royalty amount and the recoup cap.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin finds the new counter unattractive, feels they cannot reach an agreement, and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin re-enters the negotiation, criticizing their previous counter-offer, and issues an ultimatum to accept his original terms immediately.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founders whisper to quickly confer on Kevin's ultimatum.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Sobhan formally accepts Kevin's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Kevin celebrates successfully closing the deal.

exchanges.label: Investor role and return on capital

decisions.note: Not a fisherman, doesn't have a feel for the product.

decisions.terms: $325,000 for 10% equity, plus a royalty of $3 per unit until $1,000,000 is recouped.
decisions.note: Wants a creative way to get his capital back since they are mostly a product.
Disagrees with their philosophy that success is about who you know, thinks they have a long way to go.
Struggles with the high valuation, requiring massive sales to make a return.
Counters Kevin's royalty offer with a straight equity deal.

decisions.terms: $325,000 for 10% equity, plus a royalty of $1.50 per unit until $500,000 is recouped.
decisions.note: Reduces the royalty amount and the recoup cap from Kevin's original offer.
Finds the counter-offer unattractive, feels there is no meeting of the minds.

decisions.terms: $325,000 for 10% equity, plus a royalty of $3 per unit until $1,000,000 is recouped.
decisions.note: Offers one last chance to accept his exact original terms.

record.notes: An edit at 8:18 hides the transition where Kevin decides to re-enter the negotiation after having formally exited.
